exposure: late preterm birth (34 0/7 to 36 6/7 weeks of gestation)
outcome: respiratory problems (transient tachypnea of the newborn, respiratory distress syndrome)
cohort: This study included 129 late preterm infants and an unspecified number of term infants born between November 2009 and October 2010.
finding: The study found that late preterm infants had significantly higher rates of hyperbilirubinemia, neonatal intensive care unit admissions, hypothermia, respiratory problems, infections, hypoglycemia, and feeding problems compared to term infants.
